header_summary:
The Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) 300 is currently vulnerable to manipulation by attackers who can influence bundle scores through ALARM messages, potentially allowing an attacker with a 26% stake to censor BIP 300 bundles indefinitely. Proposed changes include banning ALARM messages and other downvoting mechanisms to reinforce the security model back to a 75% honest majority assumption, thus aligning more closely with Bitcoin's standard of a 50% honest majority. These adjustments aim to enhance the integrity and fairness of the drivechain process, essential for secure Bitcoin transactions. [More details](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/2e554c89-a2a1-4bcf-941c-32f6a8ba9567n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m8c5a1483ce116d2f2cd883a2f4e160fc93a6bd03).

In parallel, advancements in Bitcoin's payment infrastructure are being driven by protocols like [Intents](https://docs.arkadeos.com/intents/overview), [Kaleidoswap](https://kaleidoswap.com/), and [Cassis](https://cassis.cash/), which facilitate seamless transactions across multiple layers using Hash Time Locked Contracts (HTLCs). The Cassis system, particularly, allows for offline fund reception and offers users the flexibility to balance privacy, security, and custody by selecting appropriate layers. However, the implementation, still in progress, faces challenges such as establishing a reliable reputation system for routing nodes and enhancing communication protocols. [Read more](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/cassis-a-new-simple-scheme-for-generic-multi-layer-multi-hop-htlc-routing/2952).

recent_posts.summary:
- Security risks in BIP 300 arise from score manipulation via ALARM messages.
- Proposed changes eliminate downvoting to uphold a 51% success threshold.
- Enhancements aim to strengthen drivechain process and ensure transaction security.

recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin's evolving payment landscape is boosted by initiatives like Arkade, Kaleidoswap, and Cassis.  - Cassis enables indirect payment chains for Bitcoin, improving settlement, costs, and offline transactions.  - Technical challenges remain, including standardizing node communication and securing fund reclamation.

today_in_history_posts.title: Proposed BIP for MuSig2 PSBT Fields
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- A BIP draft for MuSig2 PSBT fields has been written and posted on GitHub.
- The draft modifies the original gist by using compressed pubkeys.
- It is based on Sanket's gist but keys participant pubkeys by the aggregate xonly key.

today_in_history_posts.title: Removing channel reserve for mobile wallet users
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Removing channel reserves improves capital efficiency and user experience for wallet providers.
- Service providers cover commit transaction fees, minimizing loss risk when revoking commitments.
- The system retains security as users can display proof against dishonest service providers.
